findings.title: Retry-count deletion is not restricted to SMS reminders
findings.body: The second branch of the deleteMany OR only checks retryCount > 1, with no method, scheduled, or scheduledDate restriction. As written it deletes WorkflowReminder rows of any method (EMAIL/WHATSAPP as well as SMS) once their retryCount exceeds 1, even though this cron is only supposed to clean up SMS reminders. The SMS filter from the original query must be applied to the retry-count branch as well (or hoisted outside the OR), otherwise any present or future code that increments retryCount on non-SMS reminders will have those reminders silently deleted by the SMS cron.

findings.title: Reminders with no message or no recipient never consume a retry
findings.body: When message is empty/null or sendTo is falsy, the `if (message?.length && sendTo)` block is skipped entirely: the reminder is not marked scheduled, retryCount is not incremented, and nothing is logged. Such reminders (e.g. a booking with no smsReminderNumber) are therefore re-fetched and re-processed on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes, which is exactly the unbounded retry loop this PR claims to eliminate. This path needs to increment retryCount (or delete/handle the reminder) so it terminates after two failures.

findings.title: Retry-count update inside catch can throw and abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The catch block now awaits prisma.workflowReminder.update without its own error handling. If the original error was a database/connection problem, or the reminder was deleted concurrently, this update throws out of the for loop: all remaining unscheduled reminders are skipped and the handler never sends its 200 response. Before this change the catch only logged and continued with the next reminder. The increment should be guarded (nested try/catch) so one failing reminder cannot abort processing of the rest.

findings.title: Retry count uses stale read-modify-write instead of an atomic increment
findings.body: Both increment sites write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (or the row changes between findMany and update), both writers store the same value and a failure is lost, so a permanently failing reminder can take far more than two attempts to be deleted, or never pass the gt:1 threshold under repeated overlap. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` instead.
